From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Asha Verma <asha@curesync.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CureSync pilot: draft evaluation map & acceptance matrix

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, attached is a first-pass evaluation map for the pilot along with an acceptance matrix (attached: curesync-map-v1.xlsx). The goal is to make the acceptance path explicit so your engineers and ours have a single source of truth for: what "works", when we consider the pilot successful, and what would trigger a go/no-go.

High-level proposal (please review and flag any must-haves):
- Success criteria (candidate): 1) average latency <= 120ms P50 for common prompts, 2) model concordance >= 92% on curated prompt set, 3) embeddings vector similarity recall >= 0.95 for retrieval tasks, 4) no PII exfiltration events in security scans.
- Exit gates: canary to 1) fail if latency/regression > 20% vs baseline, 2) fail if automated tests show >5% drop in concordance on any critical prompt group.
- Acceptance tests: smoke, accuracy sweep, failover/fallback test, and SOC-related checklist. Each test has an owner and a pass threshold in the spreadsheet.

Proposed timeline: finish instrumentation & test harness by 7/16, run two-week smoke + accuracy sweep 7/19–7/30, decision window week of 8/2.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the spreadsheet and mark "must have" vs "nice to have" columns by EOD Friday 7/10.
2) We lock owners and schedule a two-hour technical kickoff the week of 7/12.

If that sounds right, I’ll ask Ben to send a calendar invite with the draft kickoff agenda and we'll update the MAP in Drive.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Quick read-through — this is helpful, thanks. A few immediate comments from the compliance and product teams:

I attached the SOC2 evidence request we typically send vendors so you can see the compliance artifacts we need (SOC2-evidence-ask.pdf).

We can meet for the technical kickoff; 7/13 morning PST works for our infra lead. I’ll mark the spreadsheet with must-haves by Friday.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Asha Verma <asha@curesync.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CureSync pilot: draft evaluation map & acceptance matrix

Asha / team —

Thanks for the quick notes, Asha. A couple of engineering clarifications and proposed pass/fail mechanics to include in the MAP:

1) Latency: our recommended test harness will run the representative prompt set at 95% CPU utilization for the GPU fleet (to mimic peak load). Pass = P50 <= 120ms AND P95 <= 380ms over a rolling 24h window for the smoke run. Failure = sustained P95 > 500ms or >20% regression vs baseline.

2) Concordance: we’ll provide the curated prompt groups (clinical / non-clinical). For clinical group we’ll require >=95% at 95% confidence. We’ll also run stratified A/B sampling to ensure no hidden bias.

3) Drift & monitoring: schedule daily drift job + automated alert to your Slack channel when posterior probability of distribution shift > 0.04. We’ll include a runbook for manual triage in the spreadsheet.

4) Security: we can confirm encrypted logs and 30-day retention; please confirm whether CureSync requires HSM-backed key ownership (we support both customer-managed KMS and Redwood-managed keys).

I’ve added the proposed numeric thresholds into the "Acceptance tests" tab of the MAP and put owner tags. If you want, I can push a short demo of the instrumentation during the kickoff.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the feedback and glad the timing works. Per Marissa/Karthik's updates, here's what Redwood will deliver and the next formal steps so we have a single-track close cadence:

- Instrumentation + test harness (Karthik) — in place by 7/16.
- Acceptance test runbook + sprint plan (Marissa) — draft by 7/12, final by 7/18.
- SOC2 evidence bundle (Security Ops) — upload to your secure bucket by 7/15.

Mutual action items for CureSync
- Mark must-have columns in MAP spreadsheet by 7/10 (confirmed from Asha).
- Provide KMS preference (customer-managed or Redwood-managed) by 7/12.
- Confirm kickoff participants and time slot (we propose 7/13 10:00–12:00 PST).

Acceptance & decision timing
- Smoke + accuracy sweep: 7/19–7/30.
- Decision window (final review and sign-off): week of 8/2.

We’ll also send over a DocuSign statement of work for the pilot (DocuSign link) and a finalized MAP export after the kickoff. If everything is green in the run, we expect to be able to present a recommendation to our leadership the week of 8/9.

I’ll attach the finalized MAP after Asha confirms the must-haves.

Best —
